newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's population up 5.7 pct in last five years.
newsitem.headline: Canada's population up 5.7 pct in last five years.

text.p: The population of Canada, a favourite destination for emigrants from other countries, grew by 5.7 percent in the last five years to 28.8 million but the rate of growth has fallen, according to a census released on Tuesday.
The government agency Statistics Canada said that Canada, at 1.1 percent, had the highest annual population growth rate of any nation in the Group of Seven major industrialised democracies.
The census, the first in five years, was taken in May 1996 and showed Canada's population had doubled since 14 million were counted in 1951. The population figure stood at 28,846,761 as of May 14.
Half of the growth over the last five years was due to immigration and half to natural increase, defined as births minus deaths.
Canada, the world's second largest country in terms of area, has one of the highest immigration rates, though it has declined in recent years largely as the result of government restrictions.
The 5.7 percent population growth was down from 7.9 percent between 1986 and 1991, when immigration was significantly higher, Statistics Canada officials said.

During the latest five-year period, booming British Columbia showed the highest growth at 13.5 percent. Ontario grew by 6.6 percent and Alberta by 5.9 percent. Even Quebec grew by 3.5 percent, despite separatist rumblings.
The depressed Atlantic provinces showed a rate ranging from minus 2.9 percent for Newfoundland, as people left the province, to plus 3.7 percent in tiny, touristy Prince Edward Island.

The prairie provinces have struggled to maintain their populations as farms get bigger and people move to more promising jobs. Saskatchewan had shown a loss at the last census and grew by only 0.1 percent this time, while Manitoba grew by 2.0 percent.
Toronto became the first Canadian metropolitan area with more than four million people. Its population grew 9.4 percent to 4.3 million.
Metropolitan Montreal added 3.7 percent, to 3.3 million, while Vancouver jumped 14.3 percent to 1.8 million. The Ottawa region topped one million for the first time, growing 7.3 percent.
